name: A Killer Game On The Screen (home switch, cages drawn, killer record only; 13 languages)
note: Written with the gate on 2026-10-01. Each mutation breaks one thing a killer player sees.

mutations.name: a killer's Speedrun tab switches instead of saying it is coming
mutations.why: The tab sets the home mode silently. On the killer card nothing seems to happen — the card still plays Classic, because a kind without the mode plays its first one — so the player taps a tab that does nothing visible and is never told why. First written expecting "changed the mode"; that cannot happen here for the reason just given, and the gate failed on the missing note instead.

mutations.name: the ⓘ shows for killer only again
mutations.why: The user's complaint: with the ⓘ on one kind only, the switch changed width when the kind changed and the layout broke. First written with the hidden attribute, which changed nothing: .rival-info-btn sets display: flex, and an author display beats the browser's [hidden] rule — it survived for that reason.
mutations.replace: <button type="button" style={{ display: variant === 'killer' ? undefined : 'none' }} className="rival-info-btn variant-rules-btn"

mutations.name: the killer card drops the mode tabs
mutations.why: How the first version did it: the card lost a row on killer and jumped in height every time the kind changed. First written with the hidden attribute, which .mode-tab-group's display: grid overrides; it survived for that reason.

mutations.name: the Ghost chip on killer shows its own note
mutations.why: Two notes stacked in the same place at the bottom of the screen, one saying the rival is locked until a level is cleared — which is not the reason on killer.

mutations.name: a cell stops drawing the right side of its cage
mutations.why: Two cages side by side merge into one dashed shape; the player reads the wrong cells into a sum.
mutations.find: if (!right) lines.push([b, up ? 0 : a, b, down ? 100 : b]);
mutations.expectFailure: no line against the next cage

mutations.name: the sums are not drawn
mutations.why: Without the number in the corner a killer is a classic puzzle with almost no givens — unsolvable.

mutations.name: Resume ignores the kind of the saved game
mutations.why: The standard switch offers to resume a killer, and the player lands in a killer they did not ask for.
mutations.find: const isCurrentTabSaved = hasSavedGame && (savedGame.gameMode || 'classic') === mode && variantOf(savedGame) === variant;
mutations.expectFailure: the standard switch offers to resume a killer

mutations.name: the first killer starts without its rules
mutations.why: A classic player meets dashed cages and small numbers and has nothing to say the numbers are sums.
mutations.expectFailure: the first killer started without its rules

mutations.name: a killer win shows the classic grade
mutations.why: The grade's times are set for classic puzzles; a killer takes longer by design and would be graded C every time.
mutations.expectFailure: a killer win shows the classic grade

mutations.name: the switch's names are set too large to fit
mutations.why: Proves the 13-language sweep measures the switch: at this size the longer names no longer fit their half.

mutations.name: the rules lines do not wrap
mutations.why: Proves the sweep measures the rules card: an unwrapped rule widens the card past the screen in every language. First written without !important, and it changed nothing — `text-wrap: pretty` further down the same rule sets the wrap mode back (both are shorthands for text-wrap-mode, the later one wins) — so it survived for that reason, not for a gap in the gate.
